source_name: NBS regulačný sandbox (regulatory sandbox / pieskovisko inovácií)
why_relevant: Launched early 2022 on top of the innovation hub; sandbox participants are named, licensable-in-progress fintechs — the earliest formal public signal that a new payments competitor intends to operate in SK.

source_name: NBS Prístup do platobných systémov NBS (SIPS / TARGET2-SK access rules, July 2025)
why_relevant: Access conditions document for non-bank PSPs joining SIPS/TARGET2-SK (applications open from 6.10.2025). Directly signals a structural market opening — new participant categories in SK clearing infrastructure, i.e. new competitors and new integration/vendor demand.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 11/2023 — statistical reporting on payment services (cards, terminals, fraud)
why_relevant: Defines the quarterly reporting templates resident PSPs must file on payment transactions, cards, terminals by device type and payment schemes. Establishes exactly what card/terminal market data exists at NBS — the schema behind any published SK acquiring/terminal statistics, which is directly relevant to a POS/terminal vendor lens.

source_name: NBS Správa o inovačnom hube a regulačnom sandboxe (annual innovation hub report)
why_relevant: Annual report on the NBS innovation hub and regulatory sandbox — describes the kinds of fintech propositions, business models and technologies firms brought to the regulator. A rare regulator-side window on the SK fintech pipeline before those actors appear in registers.

source_name: NBS Politika oversightu NBS (oversight policy PDF)
why_relevant: The Bank Board-approved oversight policy for payment systems and payment instruments — the doctrinal document behind NBS supervision of SIPS/TARGET2-SK and card/e-money instruments. Explains scope, escalation and assessment cadence.

source_name: Ministerstvo spravodlivosti SR — RPVS service page and FAQ
why_relevant: Authoritative explanation of RPVS scope, thresholds and obligations — needed to interpret absences correctly (a vendor missing from RPVS may simply be below threshold, not absent from public contracts). Also links onward to other justice registers.

source_name: CRZ metodika – Metodický pokyn pre zverejňovanie zmlúv v CRZ
why_relevant: Official methodology defining the metadata fields obliged entities must fill (contract number, subject, total price, parties, IČO, dates, annex linkage) and how documents are attached. It is the schema specification for any CRZ ingestion pipeline and explains recurring data-quality defects such as missing prices or free-text subjects that defeat naive keyword search.

source_name: Global Finance / Euromoney SK country awards (as republished by SK banks)
why_relevant: International award bodies issue Slovakia-specific titles (Best Bank, Best Digital Bank, Most Innovative Digital Bank in Slovakia). SK banks press-release these in detail, often naming the underlying digital platform or project — a route into vendor identification and into how banks position their tech externally.

source_name: Mastercard Awards Slovensko (scheme-run award) - via Forbes SK
why_relevant: Scheme-run annual award naming specific bank projects in payments/digitalisation/sustainability (e.g. mBank smart payment ring, UniCredit portfolio migration to Mastercard, VÚB cashback card, ČSOB anti-fraud campaign). Each citation is effectively a mini case study identifying a deployed product and, by implication, its technology supplier. Forbes SK is the publication partner, so results are archived year by year.

source_name: Forbes.sk – retail technology / self-checkout coverage
why_relevant: Business media aggregate self-checkout counts across chains (Lidl, Kaufland, Tesco ~half of transactions, Billa 52 stores) that retailers do not publish uniformly — the best cross-chain deployment benchmark found.

source_name: Denník E / Denník N – business reporting on Slovak IT suppliers' revenues
why_relevant: Independent journalism that ranks SK IT suppliers by revenue and contract capture — an editorial cross-check against vendor self-reporting, and a source of names not present on any reference page.

source_name: Slovenská sporiteľňa – list of processors / intermediaries (GDPR disclosure PDF)
why_relevant: Bank-side counterpart to vendor case studies: a legally required GDPR processor list naming actual suppliers (Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o. appears among them). Far harder for a vendor to spin, and it exposes relationships never marketed.

source_name: ACI Worldwide – Partners: Auriga SpA (partner profile page)
why_relevant: Vendor partner directory revealing the ACI–Auriga alliance; ACI's partner section is a systematic pointer to the integrator/reseller layer that would deliver ACI payments software into Slovak banks.

source_name: Asset Servicing Times – Tatra banka selects Temenos Multifonds
why_relevant: Concrete, attributable vendor-win evidence for Slovakia: Tatra banka (RBI group) selecting Temenos Multifonds for fund administration, covering Tatra Asset Management and DDS TB — exactly the incumbent-relationship proof this cell targets.

source_name: CEE Fintech Atlas – Slovak fintech ecosystem country profile
why_relevant: Regional CEE fintech mapping initiative with a dedicated SK ecosystem write-up; useful for cross-country benchmarking and for named-actor recall, though the entry found dates to 2021 and needs freshness checks.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o. (Slovak legal entity) – company/directory listing
why_relevant: Confirms Diebold Nixdorf has a Slovak operating entity (Bratislava, banknote sorters / ATM line) — the local delivery arm behind any SK bank contract; useful anchor for entity-level snowballing into registers and tenders.

source_name: European Commission — Investment Plan for Europe: Slovakia results page
why_relevant: Consolidated EFSI scoreboard for SK: counts of EIB projects and EIF agreements with intermediary banks/funds and mobilised investment. Useful as a cross-check and as a pointer into the underlying EIB/EIF deal records.

entity_name: LobbyFacts / EU Transparency Register entries for SK associations
source_name: LobbyFacts / EU Transparency Register entries for SK associations
why_relevant: Transparency-register datacards disclose association budgets, declared members, lobbying priorities and EU files followed — a cross-check on self-published member lists and on which regulatory topics associations actually spend money on.

source_name: PosAm – Tatra banka IT outsourcing reference (End User Services)
why_relevant: Slovak systems integrator's own reference page documenting that it won a Tatra banka tender for end-user IT services and took over the contract from a prior foreign provider. Concrete evidence of a competitor's incumbency and of how these private-bank tenders are run and disclosed only vendor-side.

source_name: Pravda / oPeniazoch (openiazoch.zoznam.sk) – cash-access and retail cashback reporting
why_relevant: Consumer/finance media enumerate which chains offer cash-at-checkout, limits and participating banks — the practical cross-retailer map of the cash-access layer that no single retailer publishes.

source_name: Slovak Investment Holding (SIH) / SZRB — fund-of-funds financial instruments
why_relevant: SIH, 100% owned by SZRB, manages over EUR 1bn of EU shared-management instruments and channels them through commercial banks. Its disclosures and the fi-compass case study reveal which SK financial institutions act as intermediaries and what systems/reporting obligations they must support.

source_name: Temenos success story – Raiffeisen Bank International / Tatra banka Payment Hub
why_relevant: Vendor-published case study that names Tatra banka (Slovakia) as a Temenos Payment Hub implementation inside RBI's group core-banking hub. Vendor case studies are the counterpart channel to bank disclosures and confirm incumbency at a named Slovak bank — a direct competitor-mapping datapoint.

source_name: Vendor 'partneri/členstvo' pages citing association membership (e.g. sféra, a.s.; Erste AM)
why_relevant: Vendors advertise their association memberships on their own sites; reverse-searching phrases like 'člen IT Asociácie Slovenska' or 'člen SBA' surfaces members that directories omit and confirms self-declared positioning in banking/finance.

source_name: Zverejnovanie.sk – legislation and obliged-entity guidance on contract publication
why_relevant: Reference source on the legal framework of publication duty (211/2000 Z.z., 546/2010 Z.z., 382/2011 Z.z.), including who is an obliged entity and which contract types are exempt. Needed to reason correctly about coverage: an absence in CRZ can mean 'exempt' rather than 'no contract', which materially changes any vendor-share inference.
